## Learning objectives

::: {.callout-note title="Learning objectives"}
- Define a capsule document against the adopted upstream contract
  (`apiVersion: open-engineering.io/v1alpha1`, `kind: Capsule`,
  memo1 §1 required fields).
- Validate it against the upstream `capsule.schema.json` with a
  JSON Schema 2020-12 validator, and see one upstream invalid
  fixture fail for the stated reason.
- Implement the declared capability in a single stdlib Python
  function behind its `spec.inputs`/`spec.outputs`, including a
  structured error on a missing required input.
- Test the implementation with `unittest`, including a contract
  test that reads the capsule document and asserts each declared
  input/output name and type is honoured.
- Compose the capsule into a minimal Pico definition using
  `spec.capabilities: [oe.greeting@0.1.0]` and validate the Pico
  against the Academy's `definitions/pico.yaml`.
- Resolve the Pico's capability requirement against the capsule
  **by hand**, applying memo2 §2 D2 (SemVer / caret / `0.x`) and
  memo2 §3 D3 (grammar), and record the result in the shape of
  the upstream `fixtures/scenarios/resolve-greeting.yaml` scenario.
:::

## Prerequisites

::: {.callout-note title="Prerequisites"}
- A working shell (bash or zsh).
- A text editor and comfort reading YAML and Python.
- **Python 3.8+** on your `PATH`.
- The Python packages `jsonschema` and `pyyaml` (install with
  `python3 -m pip install jsonschema pyyaml`).
- `curl` on your `PATH` for `solution/fetch-upstream.sh`.
- A local clone of this repository.
- Completion of the
  [Pico · Part 1 · Introduction](../../courses/pico/part-1/01-introduction/index.html)
  lesson and the [Hello Pico](../hello-pico/index.html) lab (or
  equivalent).
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Not needed"}
This lab needs no database, broker, AI library, bot platform, or
Kubernetes. There is no runtime to launch and no network service to
reach beyond `raw.githubusercontent.com` for the one-off upstream
fetch.
:::

## Environment

- Operating system: macOS, Linux, or WSL.
- Required tools: bash or zsh, Python 3.8+, `curl`, and a text editor.
- Estimated time: **45–60 minutes**.

## One-time setup

From a fresh shell, clone the Academy source repository (if you have
not already), install the two Python dependencies, and move into the
lab directory:

```bash
git clone <academy-source-repo-url> oea
cd oea
python3 -m pip install --user jsonschema pyyaml
cd labs/greeting-capsule
```

**Placeholders**

- `<academy-source-repo-url>` — the clone URL of the Open Engineering
  Academy source repository you were given access to.
